mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) or Consular Legalization if the country of origin is not a Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for every foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French translation into French/English

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, authorized agents and protected parties against: (1) the Canadian Economic Sanctions List and Consolidated Sanctions List issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (2) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions if any U.S. nexus exists; (3) UN Security Council sanctions lists; and (4) FINTRAC and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for non-resident limited partners, high-risk source jurisdictions, and any individual identified as a PEP. Ongoing transaction monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC, and record-keeping under the PCMLTFA are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online portal at www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The business name must be in French. A name in another language may be used only if accompanied by a French version and is otherwise permitted under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR, c. C-11). For a limited partnership, the required legal element is "société en commandite" (or "L.P." / "Limited Partnership" in the English version, if the name is used in English). The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must include the required legal element in the applicable script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for review with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days, attaching a fresh name-search statement and an explanation of compliance with the naming regulations. If the REQ confirms the rejection, judicial review may be pursued before the Court of Québec (Civil Chamber) under the applicable rules of administrative law. A name reservation cannot be extended after its 90-day validity period; a new reservation and fee payment are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible for the registered office of the limited partnership itself, provided it is a physical address in Quebec and not solely a post-office box. However, for the underlying commercial mail receiving business (CMRA and digital scanning), the registered business address must house active mail-handling and scanning operations; a purely nominal virtual address without physical mail handling will not satisfy the Quebec consumer protection and anti-money laundering expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annualized inspection risk: 25-30% for the registered office; 45-55% for the operating CMRA site due to statutory licensing oversight, consumer protection supervision, and FINTRAC-related AML inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2259 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 20, 25-32
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Limited partners may contribute money, property, or industry; no escrow account is required unless the partnership contract expressly stipulates such a condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the limited partnership named [LP Name] be constituted under the Civil Code of Québec and that the partnership contract be approved. Each limited partner's capital contribution is accepted as recorded in the subscription schedules. The registered office of the partnership is established at [Registered Office Address], Québec. The General Partner is vested with full management authority, and [Name] is appointed as manager/officer with power to open bank accounts, sign agreements, and file all statutory declarations. The resolution is effective immediately, and any acts taken in implementation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search through the REQ online system using the proposed French or bilingual name. Submit a reservation request for the limited partnership name and obtain a search report confirming no confusingly similar registered name. Ensure the name includes 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' as required by Québec law.
required_dossiers: Identification of the general partner and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name declaration with the REQ, addressing the objections specified in the refusal notice and providing additional supporting evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary's office and Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) setting out capital contributions, profit sharing, management authority, and the limited liability status of limited partners. Execute the Déclaration d'immatriculation containing the partnership name, head office in Québec, general partner's name and address, and the object of the partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, amend the rejected clauses, obtain fresh signatures, and resubmit through the REQ online amendment service within the statutory response period to avoid reinstatement fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Statutory Declaration and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Registration through the REQ online portal and pay the applicable registration fee. Attach the partnership agreement and proof of identity of the general partner. Upon acceptance, obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the official certificate of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected for incomplete information, correct the stated deficiencies, pay any administrative penalty, and resubmit electronically. The declaration is deemed effective upon full compliance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Québec Establishment and Municipal Business Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and local municipal permit office (e.g. Ville de Montréal or Ville de Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership's principal establishment in Québec through REQ, including the exact civic address where mail scanning and virtual office services will be provided. Apply for the municipal business permit covering a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) and virtual office operation, and complete any zoning certificate requirements for office uses.
required_dossiers: Proof of lease or ownership of the establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or permit approval is refused, initiate a variance request or modify the premises to conform to municipal by-laws; alternatively, select a compliant establishment and file a change of establishment address with REQ and the municipality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with Revenu Québec for the Québec sales tax (QST) and, if applicable, with the Canada Revenue Agency for the GST/HST. Provide the NEQ number, partnership business address, and expected revenue bracket. Apply for employer accounts if the partnership will hire staff.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, file a formal explanation with supporting partnership documents and use the online secure messaging services of Revenu Québec and CRA to rectify any inconsistencies within the prescribed time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Service de l'administration et des permis, local municipality (e.g. Ville de Montréal or Ville de Québec); Registraire des entreprises du Québec for establishment notification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'entreprise de réception de courrier commercial (Commercial Mail Receiving Agency Operating Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative office activity; no mandatory environmental impact assessment or registration required under the Schedule to the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) for virtual office and mail scanning operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; all sanitary sewage must comply with municipal sewer by-laws. No VOC-emitting processes or fuel-burning equipment used in the scanning operation. Waste paper and packaging must be recycled through commercial waste collection channels; any hazardous electronic waste (e.g. toner cartridges) must be handled under Québec's residual hazardous materials regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire safety department confirming compliance with the Québec Building Code and National Fire Code for means of egress, smoke detection, and portable extinguishers; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance verifying a hazard prevention program for employees; accessibility certificate for commercial premises receiving the public where applicable under the Québec government accessibility standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) for the federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account; Revenu Quebec (Quebec Revenue Agency) - clic RQ portal and Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) for the Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ) and QST registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident limited partnership (LP) carrying on a virtual-office/CMRA service in Quebec: (1) appoint a designated representative or agent in Canada; (2) obtain the federal BN using form RC1 or via CRA's Business Registration Online, including the GST/HST program account (RT prefix); (3) register the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec to obtain the NEQ and satisfy mandatory legal publicity (the statutory license for carrying on an enterprise in Quebec) using forms RQ-1/RQ-2 and, where acting through an agent, the power of attorney form LM-101-V; (4) register for QST with Revenu Quebec through clic RQ, obtaining the TQ account, because the LP makes taxable supplies in Quebec; (5) file annual GST34 / TPZ-14 returns online and, as a fiscally transparent partnership, file T2042 / TP-600 partnership information returns so each partner (resident or non-resident) is allocated income; (6) non-resident partners should obtain Canadian individual/corporate TINs where required and apply under treaty for withholding rate reductions; FINTRAC registration is also assessed because virtual office services may be incidental to money transmission or specified services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election. Available elections include: ITA s.249.1(3) fiscal-period election for the LP to use an off-calendar year-end; ITA s.216(1) election for a non-resident partner receiving Canadian-source rental or service income to file a Canadian return instead of being subject to full Part XIII withholding; treaty-based re-characterization of the LP as a non-entity (component member) under the Canada-US Treaty, with Form NR301/TP-1016R to claim reduced withholding; GST/HST joint election under ETA s.273 for closely related entities, and the corresponding QST election under QSTA s.557.2 where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_license_notes: The CMRA activity requires an annual declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec and, where the LP uses a virtual office, the NL/LLP must maintain a physical registered office and registered agent in Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered by CRA, together with Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) administered by Revenu Quebec as a separate provincial tax; Quebec is not a Harmonized Sales Tax participating province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in any four consecutive calendar quarters for federal GST/HST small-supplier exemption; for QST, CAD 50,000 over four consecutive quarters where the supplier is not resident in Quebec and has no establishment there. Once the virtual-office and mail-scanning fees exceed either threshold, the LP must register with CRA and Revenu Quebec; registration can be voluntary below the thresholds but is advisable to claim input tax refunds (ITC/QST-R) on start-up costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec have no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST returns (NETFILE/XML via CRA) for registrants with over CAD 1,000,000 in annual revenue and for QST large enterprises through clic RQ. Voluntary B2B e-invoicing follows the pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 framework. Invoices must meet ETA s.221 and QSTA s.444 requirements: vendor name, BN and QST registration number, date, description, consideration, and tax charged. Electronic invoices and source documents must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST/HST/QST applies to goods physically exported from Canada by the LP and delivered outside Canada to a non-resident (Schedule VI Part I of the Excise Tax Act; QSTA s.107.1). For services such as virtual-office mail scanning supplied to a non-resident client, zero-rating applies under the offshore services rules of ETA Schedule VI Part V (s.7 and s.9) and equivalent QSTA provisions where the service is provided otherwise than to persons resident in Canada, is not performed in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property, and is for the recipient's use or enjoyment outside Canada. The LP must establish the non-resident status of each client (residence certificate, jurisdiction of incorporation) and demonstrate the service is not taxable in Canada under the place-of-supply rules; zero-rated export supplies also preserve ITC/QST-R eligibility for Canadian inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A or CERS e-certified report) for any tangible goods shipped; for mail-scanning services, the equivalent service contract, statement of work, and scan/delivery activity log evidencing offshore provision for the non-resident recipient

Transport document (bill of lading, air waybill, or courier receipt) where goods are exported; for digital mail-scanning services, technology logs documenting server location outside Canada or delivery outside Canada

Inward remittance and foreign-exchange evidence (bank SWIFT MT103 or Canadian Schedule I bank exchange record) proving proceeds are received from the non-resident, retained with the LP's non-resident status file (residence certificate, Form NR6, CRS/KYC records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec can reassess within 4 years of a normal assessment, and without limitation where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud exists. If zero-rating is denied, the LP is liable for 5% GST plus 9.975% QST on the full consideration, with daily compound interest. Additional penalties include: 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month (max 10%) under ETA s.280(1); 25% penalty for false statements or omissions (s.285(1)(a)); 50% gross-negligence penalty under s.285(1)(c); and for willful evasion under s.327(1), a fine of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment. Revenu Quebec applies mirror sanctions under QSTA ss.1021.13-1031 and may cancel QST registration, deny refunds, and refer criminal prosecutions in export-fraud schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), the central monetary authority established under the Bank of Canada Act. Canada maintains no centralized foreign-exchange-control administration; the Currency Act establishes a free-floating Canadian dollar. Cross-border currency transaction surveillance is effected by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for physical currency reporting. Prudential supervision of domestic systemically important banks is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. No exchange-control approvals, no counterparty or tenor restrictions, and no restrictions on profit repatriation apply to a Quebec limited partnership. Remittances of Canadian-source business income to a foreign limited partner are not FX-gated, but the partnership must withhold 15% of the non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source business income under subsection 227(8.3) of the Income Tax Act as prepayment of Part I tax, and 25% under Part XIII (treaty-reduced, e.g., 15% to 0% under the Canada-US and Canada-UK Treaties where applicable) on interest, rents, royalties, and management-type fees remitted to non-resident partners; NR4 information returns and accompanying remittances are due to the Canada Revenue Agency. Current-account payments for the CMRA services (virtual-office and mail-scanning subscription fees remitted offshore) are unrestricted and require no governmental permit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada abolished statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements with the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951. A Quebec LP may retain service and export receipts in any freely convertible currency in Canada or abroad. However, every Canadian financial institution must report cross-border electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC, individuals and entities must declare physical currency of C$10,000 or more at the border under the CBSA regime, and all remittances must be screened against Canada's sanctions framework (Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Criminal Code terrorist-financing lists).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD); Capital Escrow / Subscription Account
Operational Account (CAD); Capital Escrow / Trust Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM as primary treasury domicile; MEDIUM as auxiliary collection rail. Canada does not operate an 'electronic money institution' (EMI) licensing category. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Mercury) may transmit funds and issue payment instructions through licensed Canadian partners, but they cannot open deposit accounts in the LP's name, issue Canadian institution/transit numbers, or provide Schedule I banking services without a Canadian bank charter. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (in force since November 2024, supervised by the Bank of Canada), payment service providers — including Stripe Canada in respect of the target rails (Stripe Recurring, Credit Card) — must register; using such providers to collect subscription revenue is structurally viable, but the LP's statutory treasury, capital accounts, and Part XIII withholding obligations must remain anchored at a Canadian Schedule I bank or at Desjardins.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Quebec société en commandite (limited partnership) is not a legal person under the Civil Code of Québec; account opening is effected by the general partner. In practice, Schedule I banks require the general partner's authorized signatories to appear in person at a Canadian branch, or to complete a FINTRAC-compliant 'dual process' remote identification with a video interview and notarized/certified identity documents. The onboarding package must include: (i) the declaration of registration (immatriculation) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ number); (ii) a certified copy of the notarized partnership agreement; (iii) identification and 25%-or-greater beneficial-ownership verification of every general and limited partner; (iv) a valid resolution or pouvoir delegating signing authority; and (v) for the CMRA scope, the municipal business licence (permis) and Revenu Québec GST/QST registration. National Bank of Canada and Desjardins offer the most efficient Quebec-based onboarding; remote opening with a mandatory video interview is permissible, but a physical director visit remains the strongest onboarding de-risking measure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office / mail-scanning operator acting as registered office or correspondence conduit for unrelated third parties (shell-company facilitation red flag under FINTRAC business-model typologies).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) valid municipal business licence and Revenu Québec GST/QST registration evidencing a regulated commercial mail-receiving agency; (ii) executed master service agreements with each mail-scanning client; (iii) a client-KYC file for each client containing identity, 25%-or-greater beneficial ownership, and stated business purpose; (iv) written attestation that the LP holds no client funds, provides no nominee-director or nominee-shareholder services, and merely scans and digitizes correspondence; (v) the LP's partner register with ultimate beneficial ownership; (vi) a written AML/ATF program, risk assessment, and sanctions/PEP screening policy; and (vii) if FINTRAC registration applies, the current MSB registration certificate (not anticipated for pure CMRA operations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding 25% or more with an opaque chain of ownership (enhanced due diligence triggered by subsection 227(8.3) Part XIII withholding and the Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (LPR) reporting).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) notarized or certified passports and proof-of-address for every 25%-or-greater partner; (ii) a full organizational chart from each ultimate beneficial owner to the LP; (iii) certified capital-contribution ledgers with source-of-funds statements (six months of bank statements); (iv) executed treaty-benefit self-certifications (IRS Form W-8BEN / W-8BEN-E for US partners and CRA Form NR6/NR7 where withholding reduction is sought) plus tax-indemnity clauses in the partnership agreement; (v) audited or review-engagement financial statements of the general partner; and (vi) a written explanation of the commercial purpose of the LP's capital structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party receipts suspected of being layered or structured through one operating account (money-mule / structuring alert for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced CMRA).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) segregated client sub-ledgers reconciled monthly to contracted fixed fees; (ii) accounting evidence that virtual-office and mail-scanning charges are fixed fees and not payment intermediation; (iii) the merchant-processing agreements and settlement statements from Stripe (Stripe Recurring) and the card acquirer; (iv) sample contracts and invoices demonstrating that each receipt matches an issued invoice; (v) the LP's no-client-funds attestation; and (vi) an independent AML/ATF risk assessment prepared by a licensed Canadian compliance consultant (CPA or former FINTRAC professional).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident partners are executed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank transfers) to the LP's Canadian account at National Bank of Canada or Desjardins. The wire must carry the LP's full legal name and NEQ number, and the remitter must complete the purpose-of-payment field with clear capital-contribution language (e.g., 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' in SWIFT Field 70) consistent with the receiving bank's balance-of-payments classification and the partnership's capital-call notice. The LP must maintain the partnership agreement, capital-call notices, subscription documents, and the partner's source-of-funds evidence; the Canadian bank will verify these documents for FINTRAC EFT reporting (C$10,000-or-more threshold) and sanctions screening. No Bank of Canada authorization is required. Foreign-currency receipts may be held as-is, converted through a spot FX trade booked with the bank's treasury desk, or hedged by forward; booking records must be preserved to support the LP's capital ledger and to preclude recharacterization as taxable income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic vendor payments clear through Payments Canada (the Automated Clearing Settlement System, ACSS, and the Real-Time Rail, RTR). Cross-border supplier disbursements use SWIFT MT103 wires containing the beneficiary's SWIFT/BIC and account details (or US ABA routing for USD). Commercial letters of credit, issued under UCP600 by the LP's bank, are used only for physical goods purchases (e.g., scanning hardware or paper) and require presentation of conforming invoice, packing list, and transport documents. The target merchant-collection rails (Stripe Recurring and credit card) settle through Stripe's Canadian licensed payment entity into the LP's CAD account via ACH/EFT credit. All outbound wires must undergo OFAC/CFT and Canada sanctions screening. Profit distributions to foreign limited partners are remitted by SWIFT MT103 net of subsection 227(8.3) and Part XIII withholdings, with NR4/T5013 slips and CRA remittance vouchers issued; the LP must file the corresponding Quebec information returns with Revenu Québec.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts booked with a Schedule I Canadian bank treasury desk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies where deliverable forwards are unavailable
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term non-resident capital protection
Vanilla FX options (European-style put/call) hedging known subscription receipts and distribution obligations
Commercial FX forwards under the bank's standard ISDA 2002 master agreement or FX master agreement, with no statutory limits on tenor or counterparty in Canada
OTC derivatives trade-reporting to the Canadian Securities Administrators' recognized trade repository only if the LP meets major-counterparty thresholds (not expected at the CMRA LP scale)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour annuelle) to the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each annual anniversary of the limited partnership's registration in the REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty plus statutory interest; after formal notice, failure to regularize the declaration can result in the Registrar striking the partnership registration from the enterprise register, with consequential loss of legal person capacity and exposure to fines under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary/Slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: by March 31 of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal period: by the last day of the first month following the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of CAD 10 per day up to CAD 1,000 for the T5013 Summary; extended non-compliance may trigger deemed information penalties, prosecution, or arbitrary assessment of partnership allocations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed solely on revenue, asset, or partner-count thresholds under Quebec law. A mandatory independent audit may be required if the partnership agreement so provides, a court orders an audit on the application of a limited partner, the partnership is a reporting issuer, or the partnership is in a regulated sector such as insurance, securities, or financial services where the regulator mandates audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada Handbook, or IFRS where the partnership or any partner is publicly accountable or the partnership agreement elects IFRS; tax accounting must also satisfy the Quebec Taxation Act and the federal Income Tax Act re: partnership allocations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a separate annual public UBO filing for limited partnerships. The general partner must review the register of partners before the REQ anniversary date, record all transfers of partnership interests in the register of transfers, verify the identity and allocation percentage of each partner for T5013 Schedule 50 reporting, and update the REQ annual declaration for any changes concerning the general partners or registered office. Limited partners' residential particulars are not publicly registered in Quebec.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the General Partner and Partners' Resolutions
Beneficial Ownership and Partner Allocation Schedule

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$200–US$900 per year for a Quebec registered office and mail-forwarding address service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500–US$10,000 per year for a small-to-mid-market limited partnership with an uncomplicated partner and transaction structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined Quebec provincial (11.5%) and federal (15%) corporate income tax rate for a general limited partnership deemed to be a corporation for Canadian tax purposes, where applicable; otherwise, the LP is fiscally transparent and tax is levied at the partner level. For non-resident corporate partners receiving Canadian-source income through the partnership, the applicable federal Part I rate is 15% plus Quebec provincial levy on allocated Quebec-source income, subject to treaty relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to commercial mail receiving agency and digital scanning activities. Eligible deductions include the Quebec Production Services Tax Credit (only for film/audiovisual, not applicable), the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit for qualifying digital R&D, and the federal Small Business Deduction only if the partner is a Canadian-controlled private corporation and the partnership interest is not held by a public corporation or non-resident-controlled entity. The Quebec Business Investment (essence) tax credit does not apply to mail scanning. A limited partnership is not a taxpayer for Quebec tax purposes; each partner computes income at the partner level. Non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII and Quebec withholding taxes on allocated income unless treaty-reduced.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec CO-17 (Sociétés) via Revenu Québec's Mon dossier d'entreprise; Canada Revenue Agency T2 Corporation Income Tax Return via CRA My Business Account; T5013 Partnership Information Return for partnerships with Canadian-resident partners or Canadian-source income; NR6 form for non-resident partner withholding election
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; instalments may be required quarterly for large partnerships or partners with prior-year tax liability
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal period ending in a calendar year, the Quebec corporate return (CO-17) is due no later than the last day of the six months following the fiscal year-end. The federal T2 is due no later than six months after the fiscal year-end. The T5013 Partnership Information Return is due by the partnership's filing due date, generally no later than five months after the fiscal year-end. Non-resident partners subject to Part X III withholding must file a T5013 schedule and remit withholding on a monthly basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income or loss from partnership activities allocated to partners; for the virtual office and mail scanning business, gross revenue from subscription and mail scanning services, operating expenses (rent, software, labour, depreciation), and net income or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Canadian-source business income allocable to the jurisdiction of the non-resident partner; attach Form T2036-NR (Information Return for Non-Resident Persons) and T5013 Summary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source partnership income subject to Part XIII withholding or Part I tax under the treaty article applicable to business profits (Article VII of the Canada-United States tax treaty or applicable DTA).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide a completed Form NR301 (Canada) or Quebec Form TP-1016-V to reduce or exempt withholding; the partnership must withhold 15% federal and 5.75% Quebec on allocated net income unless the partner is treaty-exempt and files Form NR302 or a waiver.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Revenu Québec CO-17 Line 180 (Provincial taxable income) and Line 240 (Provincial tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For a partnership that is a 'commercial partnership' under Quebec Civil Law and has a juridical personality only for specific purposes, Revenu Québec requires a CO-17 only if the partnership is a 'corporation' for tax purposes; otherwise each partner reports their share on CO-17 or TP-1 Individual Tax Return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must file a Quebec CO-17 if carrying on business in Quebec through a permanent establishment; otherwise, file a Quebec TP-1 or corporate return for allocated Quebec-source income and claim treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CRA T2 Line 600 (Balance due) / T2 Line 601 (Refund)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate tax balance where the LP is fiscally transparent: the partnership itself files a T5013, not a T2. The T2 is filed by each corporate partner. This line is used only if the LP has made the election under section 10 of the limited partnership Act to be treated as a corporation for Alberta-type jurisdictions; Quebec LPs cannot elect corporate status for federal tax purposes; hence T2 is filed by the corporate general partner or the non-resident corporate limited partners with permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner with a permanent establishment in Canada files a T2, reports its share of partnership income as business income, and claims a foreign tax credit or treaty relief for Quebec taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of management fees or administrative fees paid to a non-arm's length non-resident person, including fees paid to the virtual office platform's parent company for software licensing, data hosting, or centralized scanning services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These amounts may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax of 25% unless reduced by treaty to 5% or 0% for 'management fees' only if reasonable and not constituting royalties; Canada typically treats management fees as income from services under treaty business profits, not subject to withholding if no permanent establishment, but Quebec may require TP-80 withholding. Recharacterization risk is high; documentary evidence of arm's length nature and economic substance required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for a T5013 or T2 is CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500 (T2) or CAD 2,000 (T5013 generally, higher for large partnerships). Revenu Québec late filing penalty is 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months, minimum CAD 100. Failure to remit withholding tax for non-resident partners incurs 10% gross negligence penalty plus arrears interest, and directors of the general partner are personally liable for unremitted withholdings under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and section 34 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For a Canadian limited partnership, profit distributions are not dividends; distributions of Canadian-source income to non-resident limited partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at the statutory rate of 25% (federal) plus Quebec withholding of 5.75% (total 30.75%) unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty. Under the Canada-United States tax treaty, the rate is 15% on actual 'dividends' but for partnership distributions the rate depends on the character of the underlying income; business profits earned through a permanent establishment are taxed on a net basis (Part I) and not subject to withholding. For a pure passive distribution of non-business income, the treaty rate is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident partner must: (1) establish residency with a valid Certificate of Residence (form NR301 for Canada, or Quebec TP-1016-V for Quebec) issued by the foreign tax authority; (2) file a completed NR301 with the partnership before the distribution date or before the 30th day after the distribution; (3) submit a waiver or reduced-withholding certificate under Part XIII; (4) if tax was over-withheld, file an application for a refund using Form T1019 with the CRA and Form TP-86-V with Revenu Québec within three years of the end of the calendar year; (5) provide the partnership with a declaration of treaty benefits under the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) if the treaty is MLI-covered. For the Canada-United States treaty, the limitation on benefits (LOB) provision must be satisfied; for the Canada-Quebec domestic context, no additional treaty applies as Quebec is a subnational jurisdiction and relies on the Canada-foreign treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties paid to non-resident licensees is 25% federal plus 5.75% Quebec, reduced to 0% under the Canada-United States treaty for certain copyright royalties, 10% for industrial property royalties, and 0% for computer software royalties that qualify as 'cultural software' or 'payments for the use of computer programs' (subject to treaty interpretation). Interest paid to a non-resident arm's length lender is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax; interest to a non-arm's length non-resident is subject to 25% federal plus 5.75% Quebec unless treaty-reduced to 10%, 5%, or 0% under the Canada-United States treaty interest article (Article XI, generally 0% for arm's length, 15% for contingent interest). The virtual office business model may licence proprietary mail-scanning software to clients: cross-border royalty rates in DTAs with tax treaty partners (e.g., UK 0% for software royalties, Germany 10% for industrial royalties) must be documented and a TP-80 withholding return filed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Canadian transfer pricing rules (section 247 of the Income Tax Act), contemporaneous documentation (Local File and Master File) is required for any transaction with a non-resident non-arm's length party where the total value of the transactions exceeds CAD 1 million (aggregate for all such transactions in a taxation year). For a partnership, the threshold is applied at the partner level for transactions allocated to each partner. Revenu Québec adopts the same threshold for Quebec tax purposes (CAD 1 million). If the aggregate cross-border transactions exceed CAD 5 million, a Country-by-Country Report may be required for an ultimate parent entity with consolidated revenue over EUR 750 million; however, a virtual office/CMRA entity typically falls below this. Master File is mandatory for transactions above CAD 5 million; Local File is mandatory above CAD 1 million. Additionally, the CRA form T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions) must be filed for each transaction in excess of CAD 100,000 with a non-resident related party.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — used for mail scanning service fees charged to related customers or from related software licensors
Resale Price Method — used for a distribution/agency structure where the Canadian LP resells scanning hardware or white-label services purchased from a related non-resident
Cost Plus Method — used for intercompany provision of mail receiving, digitization, and data entry services performed in Quebec for foreign affiliates

TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — recommended as the most reliable method for a routine service provider earning a low-risk operating margin (e.g., operating margin or Berry ratio between 5% and 15%)
Profit Split Method — used if both the Canadian LP and the foreign related party contribute unique intangible assets such as proprietary scanning algorithms or client lists
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of Quebec do not exist as a separate code; Canada applies the 'general anti-avoidance rule' (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and the 'economic substance' doctrine under Quebec's anti-avoidance provision (Tax Administration Act, section 1079.2). A virtual office/mail scanning LP must demonstrate real economic substance: physical office in Quebec, employees engaged in mail reception, scanning, data processing, and client communication, substantive local decision-making by the general partner, no artificial transactions to shift income to zero-tax jurisdictions. The CRA's CRA Folio S4-F9-C1 and the OECD's BEPS Action 5 minimum standard on harmful tax practices are applicable. If the LP is a 'shell' with no employees, no physical presence, and only passive mail forwarding, the CRA may apply GAAR to reallocate income to the actual controller, impose a 10% penalty on the tax benefit, and deny treaty benefits under the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) package. For Quebec, the 'substance' requirement also affects the entitlement to the lower 11.5% provincial rate, as a corporation or partner must not be a 'specified corporate partner' without substantial Canadian presence. A partnership must also comply with the Canada Revenue Agency's beneficial ownership reporting requirements under the Canada Business Corporations Act (as amended) if it has a federal incorporation; under Quebec's registry of entreprises, a declaration of registrant (immatriculation) must list the general partner and any limited partners with 25% or more of the partnership, and the registry is publicly accessible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Failure to Report Partnership Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The general partner or a limited partner deliberately omits Canadian-source partnership income, fabricates expenses (e.g., false mail scanning equipment purchases, fake subcontractor invoices), or uses the limited partnership to channel U.S. clients' subscription fees to an offshore zero-tax jurisdiction without reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Canadian Income Tax Act (sections 238 and 239), tax evasion is an indictable offence punishable by a fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus imprisonment for up to five years. Revenu Québec under the Tax Administration Act (sections 47 and 69) imposes a civil penalty of 50% of the extra tax for gross negligence and up to 100% for wilful evasion, plus daily interest at prescribed rates (currently 10% per annum). Conviction for tax evasion also results in publication under the CRA's 'Name and Shame' program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, withheld taxes, GST/QST, and employee source deductions under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act and section 498 of the Quebec Taxation Act. For an LP with no corporate general partner, the limited partners who participate in management lose limited liability and become jointly and severally liable for partnership debts and penalties. Personal liability extends to civil restitution orders, a travel ban under the Income Tax Act section 238(2) (suspension of passport for non-payment of taxes exceeding CAD 10,000), and imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LP borrows from a non-resident limited partner or a related foreign parent using a debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 1.5:1, and pays interest that is not at arm's length; the interest is deducted in Canada, stripping taxable income from the Quebec virtual office operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 18(4) of the Income Tax Act, interest deductions are denied in proportion to the debt that exceeds 1.5 times the 'equity' of the partnership or partner. A penalty of 10% of the disallowed amount under section 247(3) applies if the taxpayer did not make reasonable efforts to document the transfer pricing. Revenu Québec may additionally reassess and impose a 20% penalty under section 1078.2. The CRA may apply the 'earnings stripping' rules under section 18(5) for excessive interest paid by a Canadian entity to a specified non-resident shareholder, disallowing the interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable for the reassessed tax, interest, and penalties only if the underpayment was a result of a misrepresentation that they knew or should have known. Criminal liability for counselling non-arm's length interest stripping can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The limited partnership is registered in Quebec solely to receive mail and scan documents, but has no employees in Quebec, no general partner with actual management functions, and the entire back-office is performed by a related entity in Delaware, U.S.A.; the Quebec entity claims the Canada-U.S. treaty exemption for business profits because it lacks a permanent establishment in Canada while simultaneously claiming Canadian tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA can deny the treaty benefits and recharacterize the Canadian entity as a permanent establishment of the U.S. parent, resulting in Part I tax at 15% (federal plus 11.5% Quebec) on a deemed net income computed by the CRA, plus a 10% GAAR penalty, and gross-negligence penalties of 50%. Revenu Québec can dissolve the registered partnership for failure to maintain the registered office in Quebec. Under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, a partnership that fails to disclose the ultimate beneficiary may be struck from the register of enterprises (Registraire des entreprises), and its directors may be personally liable for debts up to CAD 10,000 per month of unlawful operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner who signed the false declaration of registrant may be fined up to CAD 5,000 (per offence) and imprisonment for up to two years for perjury under the Quebec Legal Publicity Act. The CRA's GAAR can impose liability on the partnership itself, and if the partnership lacks assets, the general partner and its directors are liable to the extent of assets; limited partners may be held liable if they acted as agents of the partnership or allowed their names to be used in the business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering through Mail Scanning and Virtual Office
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The virtual office accepts payments (Stripe recurring, credit card) for mail scanning services from non-resident clients, but the general partner also receives cash or cryptocurrency through a mail forwarding scheme to launder funds; the business fails to register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC, fails to verify client identity, and does not report suspicious transactions or large cash payments over CAD 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, an unregistered MSB can be subject to an administrative monetary penalty of up to CAD 1,000,000 for a first offence and up to CAD 2,000,000 for a subsequent offence for an entity; individuals are liable to fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. If the business is not an MSB but a 'transaction-based' business, may still be a non-financial designated business; failure to report a suspicious transaction (STR) can lead to a penalty of up to CAD 500,000. FINTRAC can publish or suspend the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for FINTRAC penalties if they 'direct, authorize, or participate' in the contravention. Seizure of corporate bank accounts, travel bans, and extradition for money laundering under the Criminal Code (sections 462.31) can result in imprisonment of up to 10 years for individuals, and if convicted, the court may order restitution to victims and forfeiture of property. Directors of the corporate general partner may be subject to proceeds-of-crime confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Register or Hold Statutory Licence for Commercial Mail Receiving Agency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LP operates as a virtual office and mail scanning business in Quebec without obtaining the required legal publicity declaration (immatriculation) from the Registraire des entreprises, or fails to comply with Canada Post / Canada Border Services Agency rules for commercial mail receiving agencies, or fails to obtain a permit required under provincial consumer protection law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, any person carrying on an enterprise in Quebec must be registered; failure carries a fine of CAD 300 to CAD 5,000 for each day of non-compliance for a legal person, and the right to institute legal proceedings is suspended. Under the Canada Post Corporation Act, using a post office box or mail forwarding address to misrepresent a place of business is an offence punishable by up to CAD 10,000 per offence for a corporation and CAD 2,000 for an individual. Revenu Québec may deny tax deductions for unregistered enterprises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, or agents who knowingly authorized or acquiesced in the violation are liable to the penalties, and may be subject to directors' liability for any taxes, charges, or penalties under the Legal Publicity Act, including civil liability for obligations incurred while the entity was not registered.
